chunks.arabic_text: وَكَتَبَ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ إِلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ يَسْأَلُهُ:

translations.en: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id wrote to Abī al-Hasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, asking him:

chunks.arabic_text: عَنْ سَرِيرِ الْمَيِّتِ يُحْمَلُ أَلَهُ جَانِبٌ يُبْدَأُ بِهِ فِي الْحَمْلِ مِنْ جَوَانِبِهِ الْأَرْبَعَةِ أَوْ مَا خَفَّ عَلَى الرَّجُلِ يَحْمِلُ مِنْ أَيِّ الْجَوَانِبِ شَاءَ

translations.en: About the bier of the deceased being carried: is there a particular side from its four sides with which one should begin carrying, or should a man carry from whichever side is easier for him, from any side he wishes?
So he عليه السلام wrote: "From whichever of them he wishes."

en.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on carrying the bier of the deceased and asks whether one must begin from a specific side. Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام replies that one may carry it from whichever side one wishes, indicating permissibility and ease in this matter.
en.seo_question: Is there a specific side from which the bier of the deceased must be carried first?

key_terms.سَرِيرِ: the bier or coffin-frame used to carry the deceased
key_terms.جَانِبٌ: a side or lateral part of the bier
key_terms.الْأَرْبَعَةِ: the four sides of the bier
key_terms.شَاءَ: he wishes; indicating choice and permissibility
